question: Can the existing offline transactional controller prevent duplicate or over-budget guarded dummy work across restart, attempt retries and competing reservations?
requirements: Immutable campaign and task per-kind nonnegative integer work-unit limits; undeclared kinds cannot execute guarded work. Old charters/tasks missing new optional fields continue to load/redeliver unchanged.

Persistent atomic reservation before each dummy call, positive integer units, stable task-scoped call identity across attempts; terminal duplicate is read-only/non-executing, conflicting identity rejected.
Task and campaign lifetime totals count reservations across attempts and restart, including failed/unknown work. Conservative never-refund accounting is acceptable if explicit.
Unresolved work blocks automatic replacement or identity-changing bypass. Require explicit evidence to reconcile unknown status before finalizing the attempt/retrying.
Lead fencing on reservation and state transitions; atomic concurrent cap behavior. Persist immutable events and include work state in export.
Preserve money/review reserve/attempt/artifact semantics; do not imply exactly-once external side effects or live-agent integration.
scope: Small readable extension in existing contracts/controller with local dummy-work tests. No separate framework/scheduler, provider or real scientific computation.
required_checks: stable call IDs and conflicting duplicate rejection
unknown/reserved work blocks replacement until reconciliation
concurrent atomic budget or stale-lead rejection
stop_condition: One independently reviewed offline extension with bounded dummy-work demonstration, or a precise compatibility/design blocker. No live integration in this task.
